verses.text: Now Solomon had made an end of praying. Then the fire came down from heaven. It consumed (burned up) the burnt offering and the sacrifices. And the glory of the LORD filled the house (temple).
And the priests could not enter into the house of the LORD. For the glory of the LORD had filled the LORD's house.

All the children of Israel saw how the fire came down. They saw the glory of the LORD upon the house. They bowed themselves with their faces to the ground upon the pavement (stone floor). They worshipped, and praised the LORD, saying: For He is good. For His mercy endures for ever.
Then the king and all the people offered sacrifices before the LORD.
And king Solomon offered a sacrifice of 22,000 oxen, and 120,000 sheep. So the king and all the people dedicated (gave to God) the house of God.

And the priests waited on their offices (stood at their jobs). The Levites also stood with instruments of music of the LORD. David the king had made them to praise the LORD. They praised Him because His mercy endures for ever. David praised by their ministry (service). And the priests sounded trumpets before them, and all Israel stood.

Moreover (also) Solomon hallowed (made holy) the middle of the court (courtyard). It was before the house of the LORD. For there he offered burnt offerings, and the fat of the peace offerings. This was because Solomon's brasen (bronze) altar was not able to receive them. It could not hold the burnt offerings, the meat offerings (grain offerings), and the fat.
At the same time Solomon kept the feast 7 days. All Israel was with him. It was a very great congregation (crowd). They came from the entering in of Hamath to the river of Egypt.
And in the 8th day they made a solemn assembly (holy meeting). They kept the dedication of the altar 7 days. They kept the feast 7 days.

The 23rd day of the 7th month came. Solomon sent the people away into their tents. They were glad and merry (happy) in heart. It was for the goodness the LORD had showed to David and Solomon. He had showed it to Israel His people.

Thus Solomon finished the house of the LORD, and the king's house. Solomon wanted to make things in the LORD's house and in his own house. He prosperously effected (did with success) all that came into his heart.
And the LORD appeared to Solomon by night, and said to him: I have heard your prayer. I have chosen this place to Myself for an house of sacrifice.
If I shut up heaven so that there be no rain. Or if I command the locusts (grasshoppers) to devour (eat up) the land. Or if I send pestilence (deadly sickness) among My people.

If My people, which are called by My name, shall humble themselves, and pray. If they seek My face, and turn from their wicked ways. Then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin. And I will heal their land.
Now My eyes shall be open. My ears shall be attent (listening) to the prayer that is made in this place.
For now have I chosen and sanctified (made holy) this house. Then My name may be there for ever. And My eyes and My heart shall be there perpetually (always).

And as for you, if you will walk before Me as David your father walked. If you will do according to all that I have commanded you. If you will observe (keep) My statutes (laws) and My judgments (rules),
Then will I stablish (make firm) the throne of your kingdom. I covenanted (made an agreement) with David your father, saying: There shall not fail you a man to be ruler in Israel.
But if you turn away, and forsake (leave) My statutes (laws) and My commandments. I have set them before you. If you go and serve other gods, and worship them,

Then will I pluck them up by the roots out of My land. I have given it to them. And this house I have sanctified (made holy) for My name. I will cast (throw) it out of My sight. I will make it to be a proverb and a byword (something people mock) among all nations.
This house is high. It shall be an astonishment (shock) to every one that passes by it. Each person shall say: Why has the LORD done thus to this land, and to this house?

And it shall be answered: Because they forsook (left) the LORD God of their fathers. He brought them forth (out) out of the land of Egypt. But they laid hold on other gods, and worshipped them, and served them. Therefore has He brought all this evil upon them.

V15 keeps the KJV's the battle is not yours, but God's. V20 keeps Believe in the LORD your God, so shall ye be established.

verses.text: It came to pass after this also. The children of Moab and the children of Ammon came against Jehoshaphat to battle. Others beside the Ammonites came with them.

Then there came some that told Jehoshaphat, saying: There comes a great multitude (crowd) against you. They come from beyond the sea on this side Syria. And look, they are in Hazazontamar, which is Engedi.
And Jehoshaphat feared, and set himself to seek (look to) the LORD. He proclaimed a fast (announced a time of no eating) throughout all Judah.
And Judah gathered themselves together, to ask help of the LORD. Even out of all the cities of Judah they came to seek (look to) the LORD.
And Jehoshaphat stood in the congregation (crowd) of Judah and Jerusalem. He stood in the house of the LORD, before the new court (courtyard),

And said: O LORD God of our fathers, are not You God in heaven? And rule not You over all the kingdoms of the heathen (nations)? And in Your hand is there not power and might? None is able to withstand (stand against) You.
Are not You our God? You did drive out the inhabitants (people) of this land before Your people Israel. You gave it to the seed (children) of Abraham Your friend for ever.
And they dwelt (lived) in it. They have built You a sanctuary (holy house) in it for Your name, saying:

If evil comes upon us, as the sword, judgment, pestilence (deadly sickness), or famine (no food). If we stand before this house, and in Your presence. (For Your name is in this house.) If we cry to You in our affliction (trouble). Then You will hear and help.
And now, look at the children of Ammon and Moab and mount Seir. Israel came out of the land of Egypt. You would not let Israel invade them then. Israel turned from them, and destroyed them not.
Look, I say, how they reward us. They come to cast (throw) us out of Your possession. You have given it to us to inherit (own).
O our God, will You not judge them? For we have no might against this great company (army) that comes against us. Neither know we what to do. But our eyes are upon You.
And all Judah stood before the LORD. Their little ones, their wives, and their children stood there.

Then the Spirit of the LORD came upon Jahaziel. He was in the middle of the congregation (crowd). Jahaziel was the son of Zechariah, the son of Benaiah. Benaiah was the son of Jeiel, the son of Mattaniah. Jahaziel was a Levite of the sons of Asaph.

And Jahaziel said: Hearken (listen), all Judah, and you inhabitants (people) of Jerusalem, and you king Jehoshaphat. This is what the LORD says to you: Be not afraid nor dismayed (discouraged). Do not fear by reason of (because of) this great multitude (army). For the battle is not yours, but God's.
To morrow (tomorrow) go down against them. Look, they come up by the cliff of Ziz. You shall find them at the end of the brook (valley). It is before the wilderness (desert) of Jeruel.

You shall not need to fight in this battle. Set yourselves, stand still. And see the salvation (saving power) of the LORD with you, O Judah and Jerusalem. Fear not, nor be dismayed (discouraged). To morrow (tomorrow) go out against them, for the LORD will be with you.
And Jehoshaphat bowed his head with his face to the ground. All Judah and the inhabitants (people) of Jerusalem fell before the LORD. They were worshipping the LORD.
And the Levites stood up. They were of the Kohathites and of the Korhites. They praised the LORD God of Israel with a loud voice on high.

And they rose early in the morning. They went forth (out) into the wilderness (desert) of Tekoa. And as they went forth (out), Jehoshaphat stood and said: Hear me, O Judah, and you inhabitants (people) of Jerusalem. Believe in the LORD your God, so shall you be established (made firm). Believe His prophets, so shall you prosper (succeed).

And Jehoshaphat consulted with the people. Then he appointed singers to the LORD. They should praise the beauty of holiness, as they went out before the army. They should say: Praise the LORD, for His mercy endures for ever.

And they began to sing and to praise. Then the LORD set ambushments (surprise attacks) against the children of Ammon, Moab, and mount Seir. They were come against Judah. And they were smitten (struck down).

For Ammon and Moab stood up against the inhabitants (people) of mount Seir. They came utterly to slay (kill) and destroy them. And they made an end of the inhabitants (people) of Seir. Then every one helped to destroy another.
And Judah came toward the watch tower in the wilderness (desert). They looked to the multitude (army). And look, they were dead bodies fallen to the earth, and none escaped.

And Jehoshaphat and his people came to take away the spoil (riches) of them. They found among them riches in abundance (a great amount) with the dead bodies. They found precious jewels, which they stripped off for themselves. It was more than they could carry away. And they were 3 days in gathering of the spoil (riches). It was so much.

And on the 4th day they assembled (gathered) themselves in the valley of Berachah (blessing). For there they blessed the LORD. Therefore the name of the same place was called: The valley of Berachah (blessing), to this day.
Then they returned, every man of Judah and Jerusalem. Jehoshaphat was in the forefront of them. They went again to Jerusalem with joy. For the LORD had made them to rejoice over their enemies.
And they came to Jerusalem with psalteries (stringed instruments) and harps and trumpets. They came to the house of the LORD.
And the fear of God was on all the kingdoms of those countries. They had heard that the LORD fought against the enemies of Israel.
So the realm (kingdom) of Jehoshaphat was quiet. For his God gave him rest round about.
And Jehoshaphat reigned over Judah. He was 35 years old when he began to reign. And he reigned 25 years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Azubah the daughter of Shilhi.
And Jehoshaphat walked in the way of Asa his father. He departed not from it. He did that which was right in the sight of the LORD.
However, the high places (idol altars) were not taken away. The people had not yet prepared their hearts to the God of their fathers.
Now the rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, first and last, are written. Look, they are in the book of Jehu the son of Hanani. Jehu is mentioned in the book of the kings of Israel.
And after this Jehoshaphat king of Judah joined himself with Ahaziah king of Israel. Ahaziah did very wickedly.
And Jehoshaphat joined himself with Ahaziah to make ships to go to Tarshish. And they made the ships in Eziongeber.

Then Eliezer the son of Dodavah of Mareshah prophesied against Jehoshaphat. He said: Because you have joined yourself with Ahaziah, the LORD has broken your works. And the ships were broken. They were not able to go to Tarshish.

Covenant is written as agreement, as elsewhere on the site.

verses.text: Josiah was 8 years old when he began to reign. And he reigned in Jerusalem 31 years.
And Josiah did that which was right in the sight of the LORD. He walked in the ways of David his father. He declined (turned aside) neither to the right hand, nor to the left.

It was the 8th year of his reign. Josiah was yet young. He began to seek God. He sought after the God of David his father. And in the 12th year he began to purge (clean) Judah and Jerusalem. He cleaned them from the high places (idol altars), and the groves (Asherah idols). He cleaned them from the carved images, and the molten images (metal idols).

And they brake down (broke down) the altars of Baalim (the Baal idols) in his presence. And the images that were on high above them, he cut down. He brake in pieces (broke in pieces) the groves (Asherah idols). He broke the carved images and the molten images (metal idols). He made dust of them. He strewed (scattered) it upon the graves of those who had sacrificed to them.
And Josiah burnt the bones of the priests upon their altars. He cleansed Judah and Jerusalem.
He did so in the cities of Manasseh, Ephraim, and Simeon, even to Naphtali. He did it with their mattocks (picks) round about.

And Josiah broke down the altars and the groves (Asherah idols). He beat the graven images (carved idols) into powder. He cut down all the idols throughout all the land of Israel. Then he returned to Jerusalem.

It was the 18th year of his reign. Josiah had purged (cleaned) the land and the house. Then he sent men to repair the house of the LORD his God. He sent Shaphan the son of Azaliah, and Maaseiah the governor of the city. He sent Joah the son of Joahaz the recorder (official record keeper).

And they came to Hilkiah the high priest. They delivered (gave) the money that was brought into the house of God. The Levites that kept the doors had gathered it. They gathered it from Manasseh and Ephraim. They gathered it from all the remnant (rest) of Israel. They gathered it from all Judah and Benjamin. And they returned to Jerusalem.

Some workmen had the oversight (were in charge) of the house of the LORD. They put it in their hand. They gave it to the workmen that wrought (worked) in the LORD's house. It was to repair and amend (fix) the house.

Even to the artificers (craftsmen) and builders gave they it. They bought hewn stone (cut stone), and timber for couplings (joining beams). They used it to floor the houses which the kings of Judah had destroyed.

And the men did the work faithfully. The overseers (bosses) of them were Jahath and Obadiah. They were Levites, of the sons of Merari. And Zechariah and Meshullam, of the sons of the Kohathites, set it forward (led the work). Other Levites helped, all that could skill of (play) instruments of music.

Also they were over the bearers of burdens (carriers of loads). They were overseers (bosses) of all that wrought (worked) the work in any manner of service. And of the Levites there were scribes (writers), and officers, and porters (doorkeepers).
They brought out the money that was brought into the LORD's house. Then Hilkiah the priest found a book of the law of the LORD. It was given by Moses.
And Hilkiah answered and said to Shaphan the scribe (writer): I have found the book of the law in the house of the LORD. And Hilkiah delivered (gave) the book to Shaphan.
And Shaphan carried the book to the king. He brought the king word back again, saying: All that was committed to your servants, they do it.
They have gathered together the money that was found in the LORD's house. They have delivered (given) it into the hand of the overseers (bosses). They gave it to the hand of the workmen.
Then Shaphan the scribe (writer) told the king, saying: Hilkiah the priest has given me a book. And Shaphan read it before the king.
The king heard the words of the law. Then he rent (tore) his clothes.
And the king commanded Hilkiah, and Ahikam the son of Shaphan. He commanded Abdon the son of Micah. He commanded Shaphan the scribe (writer), and Asaiah a servant of the king's, saying:

Go, enquire (ask) of the LORD for me. Ask for those who are left in Israel and in Judah. Ask concerning the words of the book that is found. For great is the wrath (anger) of the LORD that is poured out upon us. It is because our fathers have not kept the word of the LORD. They did not do all that is written in this book.

And Hilkiah, and those the king had appointed, went to Huldah the prophetess. She was the wife of Shallum the son of Tikvath, the son of Hasrah. Shallum was keeper of the wardrobe (the king's clothes). Now she dwelt (lived) in Jerusalem in the college (second part of the city). And they spoke to her to that effect.
And Huldah answered them: This is what the LORD God of Israel says: Tell the man that sent you to me:

This is what the LORD says: Look, I will bring evil upon this place, and upon the inhabitants (people) of it. I will bring all the curses that are written in the book. They have read it before the king of Judah.

For they have forsaken (left) Me, and have burned incense (sweet-smelling spice) to other gods. They provoked (angered) Me to anger with all the works of their hands. Therefore My wrath (anger) shall be poured out upon this place. And it shall not be quenched (put out).
And the king of Judah sent you to enquire (ask) of the LORD. So shall you say to him: The LORD God of Israel says this about the words you have heard:

Your heart was tender, and you did humble yourself before God. You heard His words against this place, and against the inhabitants (people) of it. You humbled yourself before Me, and did rend (tear) your clothes, and weep before Me. So I have even heard you also, says the LORD.

Look, I will gather you to your fathers. You shall be gathered to your grave in peace. Your eyes shall not see all the evil I will bring upon this place. I will bring it upon the inhabitants (people) of the same. So they brought the king word again.
Then the king sent and gathered together all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

And the king went up into the house of the LORD. All the men of Judah went, and the inhabitants (people) of Jerusalem. The priests, and the Levites, and all the people went, great and small. He read in their ears all the words of the book of the agreement. It was found in the house of the LORD.

And the king stood in his place, and made an agreement before the LORD. He promised to walk after the LORD, and to keep His commandments. He promised to keep His testimonies and His statutes (laws). He would do it with all his heart and soul. He would perform the words of the agreement which are written in this book.
Josiah caused all present in Jerusalem and Benjamin to stand to it. And the inhabitants (people) of Jerusalem did according to the agreement of God. He is the God of their fathers.

And Josiah took away all the abominations (hated things) out of all the countries. They pertained (belonged) to the children of Israel. He made all present in Israel to serve the LORD their God. And all his days they departed not from following the LORD. He is the God of their fathers.
